Text: JP: alta ukuk yaka ats yaka <... kʰupa yaka ...>

Speaker: John Marr
Text: JM: he threw it away

Speaker: Joe Peter
Text: JP: yaka mash yawa

Speaker: John Marr
Text: JM: why did you hold that old skull again

Speaker: Joe Peter
Text: JP: qʰata <mamuk ukuk> mayka iskam ukuk miməlust tilixam yaka latet

Speaker: John Marr
Text: JM: you broke your brother-in-law's neck

Speaker: Joe Peter
Text: JP: mayka mamuk <kakshət/kashin> ukuk mayka aw yaka liku

Speaker: John Marr
Text: JM: it grew dark

Speaker: Joe Peter
Text: JP: yaka chaku pulakʰli

Speaker: John Marr
Text: JM: now his brother-in-law was sick

Speaker: Joe Peter
Text: JP: alta yaka aw yaka hayash sik

Speaker: John Marr
Text: JM: the wom/ the man tried to cure himself

Speaker: Joe Peter
Text: JP: kakupus ixt man yaka tiki mamuk ɬush ya<x̣>ka

Speaker: John Marr
Text: JM: he became alive again

Speaker: Joe Peter
Text: JP: yaka chaku ɬush

Speaker: John Marr
Text: JM: now the boy went home

Speaker: Joe Peter
Text: JP: alta ukuk kəlákəlá yaka ɬatwa kʰupa yaka haws

Speaker: John Marr
Text: JM: his sister gave him five buckets full of water

Speaker: Joe Peter
Text: JP: yaka ats paɬlach yaka kitɬən, qwinəm ukuk, chək...hmm chək

Speaker: John Marr
Text: JM: and he told him

Speaker: Joe Peter
Text: JP: wawa kʰupa yax̣ka

Speaker: John Marr
Text: JM: take care

Speaker: Joe Peter
Text: JP: mayka ɬush-nanich

Speaker: John Marr
Text: JM: when you come to the burning prairies

Speaker: Joe Peter
Text: JP: mayka chaku kʰupa ukuk, alta, ukuk paya ɬush-iliʔi

Speaker: John Marr
Text: JM: do not pour it out til you come to the fourth prairie

Speaker: Joe Peter
Text: JP: mayka mamuk-wax̣ pus mayka chaku ukuk {on} paya/ ɬush-iliʔi

Speaker: John Marr
Text: JM: then pour it out

Speaker: Joe Peter
Text: JP: alta mayka mash ukuk mayka chək kʰupá

Speaker: John Marr
Text: JM: now he went

Speaker: Joe Peter
Text: JP: alta yaka ɬatwa

Speaker: John Marr
Text: JM: he reached the prairie

Speaker: Joe Peter
Text: JP: yaka q'uʔ kʰupa ukuk hayash ɬush-iliʔi

Speaker: John Marr
Text: JM: it was hot

Speaker: Joe Peter
Text: JP: hayash wam yaka kʰupá

Speaker: John Marr
Text: JM: red flowers bloomed on the prairie

Speaker: Joe Peter
Text: JP: <...> ukuk ukuk ukuk pʰil t'səm <<qʰa yaka chaku s..>> chaku kʰupá

Speaker: John Marr
Text: JM: they poured water on

Speaker: Joe Peter
Text: JP: yaka mamuk-wax̣... yaka mamuk-wax̣ kʰupa ukuk chək kʰupá

Speaker: John Marr
Text: JM: one of his buckets was half empty

Speaker: Joe Peter
Text: JP: ukuk kit... ukuk ixt yaka kitɬən wik...wik saya...katsaq

Speaker: John Marr
Text: JM: he leaves the woods

Speaker: Joe Peter
Text: JP: yaka <ɬax̣> kʰupa ukuk stik <<iliʔi>>

Speaker: John Marr
Text: JM: and soon he came to another prairie

Speaker: Joe Peter
Text: JP: wik lili wəx̣t yaka chaku kʰapuk tənəs-ɬush-iliʔi

Speaker: John Marr
Text: JM: which was burning at it's end

Speaker: Joe Peter
Text: JP: yax̣ka wəx̣t kʰupa ukuk hayash paya kʰupá

Speaker: John Marr
Text: JM: he reached another prairie which was half on fire

Speaker: Joe Peter
Text: JP: pi wəx̣t q'uʔ <wəx̣t> kʰupa ixt tənəs-ɬush-iliʔi wəx̣t kʰupa paya
